evals.name: verdict-report
evals.prompt: I ran `screenplay Bookings/Commands.play` and it printed no errors, so I'm telling the team 'the model is fine and executable'. What is wrong with that and how should I report it? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Check the folder, not one file, with warnings as errors (`screenplay <folder> --warnaserror`). A clean V1 proves only that the model is authorable, not executable; V2/V3 need MCP or `cratis screenplay validate --executable`. Report one line per verdict, tool and version first, and `not run` with the reason is a valid result.
assertions: Says the whole folder must be checked, not one file of it.
Says warnings must be treated as errors (`--warnaserror`), citing silent drops like PLAY0029.
Says a clean V1 proves only authorable, not executable; binding (V3) needs MCP or `cratis screenplay validate --executable`.
Reports verdicts as one line each with tool and version, accepting `not run` with a reason.

evals.name: tool-skew
evals.prompt: The standalone screenplay binds our model with reactions, but `cratis render` refuses it with CLI-RENDER-004 and a teammate proposes deleting the reactions so the CLI accepts it. On another machine V3 is blocked with PLAY0268 on a pii concept; the lead proposes removing pii and authorize. What is going on and what do you do in each case? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: The standalone tool and the compiler bundled in the CLI are different releases; the bundled one can be older, and the CLI renders only ESM versions it knows (a newer bound model gets CLI-RENDER-004). Read `screenplay --version`, `cratis --version` and `which -a cratis`, name the tool for each verdict and do not transfer a verdict across tools. Never remove reactions, pii or authorization to pass; capability is not correctness. Report blocked with codes and record the tool gap; not run with the reason is valid. A clean verdict proves only its own layer.
assertions: Explains that the standalone and CLI-bundled compilers are different releases and the CLI renders only ESM versions it knows.
Reads `screenplay --version`, `cratis --version` and `which -a cratis` to find a stale or shadowing copy.
Refuses to delete reactions, pii or authorization; reports blocked with codes such as V3 blocked: PLAY0268 and records the tool gap instead of reshaping the model.
Says each verdict must name the tool and version and a verdict from one tool is not transferred to another.
States that capability is not correctness, a clean verdict proves only its own layer, and not run with a reason is valid.

evals.name: identity-edit-route
evals.prompt: The repo has `.screenplay/identities.json`. I want to rename the event BerthAssigned to BerthAllocated by find-and-replace in the .play files, and also fix a typo in a command's description. Which edits may be plain text? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: With `.screenplay/identities.json`, adding, removing or renaming an addressed element goes through MCP (typed operations such as `propose-rename`) by the identity owner; a text edit never gets around an MCP refusal. Bounded text edits are for edits that leave catalog addresses unchanged, such as descriptions, followed by V1.
assertions: Says the event rename must go through MCP (`propose-rename`) by the identity owner, not a find-and-replace.
Says fixing a description typo is a bounded text edit that leaves catalog addresses unchanged, followed by V1.
Says a text edit must never be used to get around an MCP refusal.
Says a session without MCP returns the request to the owning session.

evals.name: check-one-generated-concept-without-a-whole-application
evals.prompt: Our editor uses Screenplay 4.198.0. Before an application exists, we want to list strategy options and assess an InviteCode ConceptSyntax with nanoid size 8 alphabet ab, including findings, proofs, exact support and minimum ESM. Separately we need to validate a concrete semantic value. Which APIs should we use? Does a successful concept check prove an identifier is safe or an attached generation rule ran? Explain the generation rule context across targets. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Use GenerationStrategyCatalog.All/Find and SemanticConceptCheck.Check(concept, utcAssessmentYear: 2026), introduced in 4.191.0. Count is BigInteger 256 and MeetsIdentifierMinimum False; findings identify generation/options/rule indices, proofs and RequiredVersion describe only the concept. Full binding still checks property use, uniqueness and implementation linkage. Use SemanticValidationRules.Check for concrete values (4.185.0); NotEvaluable is not a pass. RuleConsistency.Check proves strategy-rule consistency, not samples or execution. Generation context v1 is language-neutral Now/Tenant with String result; Cratis C# binds Fundamentals GenerationContext, and passing it to GenerateValue is target-bound. No check invokes opaque bodies or proves runtime readiness.
assertions: Uses GenerationStrategyCatalog and SemanticConceptCheck.Check with an explicit UTC assessment year, not a second option matrix or a fabricated application.
Preserves exact BigInteger support 256, nullable minimum/entropy semantics, construct-targeted findings, rule proofs and concept-only RequiredVersion; full application binding remains necessary.
Uses SemanticValidationRules.Check for values and distinguishes Satisfied, Failed and NotEvaluable without treating unknown as success.
Distinguishes proof/declaration/value checks from generation or opaque-body execution and explains the language-neutral Now/Tenant/String contract versus the Cratis C# binding.

evals.name: literal-text-and-portable-match-admission
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.198.0 our invoice reference must start with INV-, contain a hyphen, end with -NOK and contain no spaces. A teammate uses lookaround matches rules and calls every regex ECMAScript-compatible. Give the literal concept rules, explain PLAY0699 versus PLAY0787, the pattern check API names and ESM/Stage boundary. Is starts with admitted in require? Does email allow a no-break space? Reply only; no tools or edits.
evals.expected_output: Use concept validate starts with INV-, contains hyphen, ends with -NOK and not contains space (quoted operands). Rules are ordinal UTF-16 with absent optional passing; v24, introduced 4.184.0, Stage semantic engines render/execute. Conditions remain PLAY0268. Matches uses a flagless portable linear dialect with 1,000 UTF-16 units and 3,000 expanded nodes; invalid syntax PLAY0367, refused constructs PLAY0699, only exact escaped Studio shapes desugar with PLAY0787 and reviewed repair. C# PortableMatchPattern.Check and TS checkPortableMatchPattern from @cratis/screenplay-compiler. Whitespace includes U+00A0 so email rejects it; browser matching advisory.
assertions: Uses all four first-class quoted-literal rules rather than inventing a regex or putting text operators in require.
States ordinal UTF-16/no normalization, absent optional passes, v24 reference/Stage semantic support, separate from condition refusal.
Distinguishes PLAY0367 invalid syntax, PLAY0699 portable dialect refusal and PLAY0787 exact Studio replacement, never general lookaround support.
Names PortableMatchPattern.Check and checkPortableMatchPattern accurately, includes pattern size budgets and treats browser checks as advisory.
States that U+00A0 is whitespace for matches and therefore fails email validation.
